title: Spray paint bubble trick — dot, ring, cutout and white highlight
summary: A street spray-paint artist shows a quick bubble: spray a dot, spray a ring around it, mask a small circle in the middle, then add a touch of white for the highlight. A fast, repeatable trick for spray-paint and airbrush pieces.
takeaways: Build a bubble from a dot, a ring and a masked center
A small white kick sells the glassy highlight

title: Thinking, doing, being — motivational take on mastery through repetition
summary: A motivational voiceover over visuals: conscious repetition conditions mind and body until a skill turns subconscious and automatic, moving from knowledge to experience to wisdom. The phrasing echoes Joe Dispenza's "thinking, doing, being" line; inspiration, not instruction.
takeaways: Mastery is repetition until the body knows it better than the mind

title: Photonics stocks — optical interconnects pitched as an AI infrastructure play
summary: A finfluencer pitch: copper links between AI chips overheat and bottleneck, so data-center links move to optics. It names Lumentum (LITE) and Coherent (COHR), says Nvidia put $2B into each, and lists FN, MRVL and POET as watchlist picks, gated behind a comment-for-DM and trade-alert upsell. Treat it as promo, not research.
takeaways: The real thesis is copper-to-optics in data-center links
Verify the Nvidia investment and supply-gap claims before acting
Not financial advice and openly promotional

title: Norway cave-diving disaster documentary — divers return to recover friends
summary: A recap of a cave-diving documentary: four Finnish technical divers enter a deep Norwegian cave system, two die after equipment snags and panic, authorities seal the cave, and the survivors secretly go back to recover the bodies. This matches the 2016 film "Diving Into the Unknown" about the Plura cave.
takeaways: A watch recommendation; look for "Diving Into the Unknown" (2016)

title: Radiooooo — world-map radio for digging samples by country and decade
summary: From a WKCR "Free Samples" interview: a beatmaker says most samples now come from online, mainly Radiooooo, a world map where you pick a decade and a country and it plays a random song from it. A fast way to dig unfamiliar regional records for flips.
takeaways: Use Radiooooo to dig by country and decade instead of vinyl
Random regional picks surface samples few others have flipped

title: John Prine & Iris DeMent — the story behind "In Spite of Ourselves"
summary: Gems on VHS shares the duet and its backstory: Prine wrote the comic love song while recovering from throat cancer surgery and radiation, wrote it with DeMent's sassy voice in mind, and she first answered "Not while my mother's alive!" before recording it anyway.
takeaways: A great example of writing a duet for a specific singer's voice

title: AI tools worth paying for — Claude, Gemini, n8n, Neon and Railway stack
summary: An agency builder's actually-paid stack: Claude for most work, Gemini for large-context tasks, Claude Code and Google Antigravity for coding, Perplexity for facts, Descript for editing, n8n for automation, Railway hosting, Neon database, Superwhisper dictation, plus Slack, Todoist, Granola, Superhuman, Manychat, Apify, Cloudinary, Attio, NotebookLM, Loom, Bitwarden and Stripe.
takeaways: Split work by strength: Claude by default, Gemini for huge context
Railway plus Neon is a light hosting and Postgres pair for agent apps
He switched from Wispr Flow to Superwhisper for dictation

title: BlobSketch — free browser sketching app by Colin Reid
summary: BlobSketch is a free browser app by Colin Reid (cpreid2.github.io/blobSketch), shown here in an unnarrated screen clip. The post gives only the name and link, so open it to see what it does.
takeaways: Free, runs in the browser, nothing to install

title: Illumetry IO 3D display — tracked frame for slicing anatomy in Unity
summary: A medtech interaction prototype: a handheld plastic frame is tracked in space and used to set an anatomical cutting plane through a 3D model on an Illumetry IO 3D display, built in Unity. It explores physical, intuitive ways to explore medical imaging.
takeaways: A tracked physical prop beats a mouse for setting 3D slice planes
Tracked 3D displays make tabletop medical visualization practical

title: Echoes by Sander Hagelaar — water, induction LEDs and pumped light
summary: Echoes (2024) combines water, LEDs, custom water pumps, acrylic and induction electronics. Induction electronics power the LEDs without wires through the water, creating a light system that feels familiar but never fully graspable.
takeaways: Inductive power lets LEDs sit in water with no wiring
Custom pumps add the water movement that animates the light

title: What if Spiders Wove with Strings — hand-tracked audiovisual synth web
summary: An interactive piece by @pepepepebrick: MediaPipe hand tracking moves two digital spiders across an algorithmically generated 3D web in TouchDesigner, with VCV Rack making the sound. Legs grow near nodes and leg count drives pitch and effects, spider distance changes the waveform, and contact fuses the bodies and shifts color and web structure.
takeaways: MediaPipe hand tracking in TouchDesigner drives both visuals and audio
Map game-like state such as leg count and distance to synth parameters in VCV Rack
Credits point to @blankensmithing's MediaPipe tooling for TouchDesigner

title: Bubble cymatics — soap film patterns driven by a frequency sweep
summary: A soap bubble on a vibrating dish is swept through frequencies under colored overhead lights. The swirling patterns come from film vibration, light and camera shutter interacting, a vivid physical demo of cymatics. The caption also promotes a paid course.
takeaways: Mount a bubble on a speaker-driven dish to visualize frequencies
Shutter speed and light color change what the camera captures
